To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the reactivities of the T cell‐specific monoclonal antibodies (MoAbs) were, with some exceptions, similar to previously described in healthy Caucasians; (ii) the TCR V gene segment usage is non‐random and is skewed in certain TCR V gene segments; and (iii) there was no significant correlation between the expression of certain TCR V‐specific MoAB and HLA class I, or class II, alleles.

the pattern of reactivities of anti‐TCRV‐specific MoAbs found in CD4 + and CD8 + subpopulations of peripheral blood lymphocyte of healthy Japanese subjects is in general found to correspond to that previously described in Caucasian healthy subjects.
the pattern of reactivity of the MoAbs used in the present study was in general similar to that previously described in Caucasians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of T‐cell receptors in healthy Japanese subjects, and the relationship between TCR V‐chain usage and the HLA phenotype.
the expression of the T cell receptors V gene products of peripheral T lymphocytes in healthy Japanese subjects, and the possible association between the expression and HLA class I/II alleles.
the expression of the T‐cell receptor (TCR), a cell surface molecule involved in the recognition of antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the V gene usage in healthy Japanese subjects is similar to that in Caucasians, and that the expression of V gene segments is non‐random and skewed in certain subsets.
no significant differences were detected between the Japanese and the Caucasian subjects, although some minor discrepancies were observed.
the V gene usage in healthy Japanese subjects is not different from that in Caucasian subjects, but that some subjects may have an increased usage of some V gene products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of TCR V gene segments in the peripheral blood of healthy Japanese subjects is in general similar to that in healthy Caucasian subjects and that there is no obvious association between TCR V genes and HLA class I alleles.
TCR V gene expression is not significantly influenced by HLA class I alleles in the CD4+ subset, whereas HLA class II alleles may influence TCR V gene use in the CD8 subset.
the TCR V gene repertoire of healthy Japanese subjects is similar to that of healthy Caucasian subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of TCR V gene segments in healthy Japanese subjects is not associated with HLA alleles.
the T cell receptor repertoire of healthy Japanese subjects is very similar to that of Caucasian subjects.
there are no distinct associations between the expression of TCR V gene segments and HLA class I/II alleles in the Japanese population.
